title: Browser Extensions Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to secure browser extensions, audit permissions, and maximize privacy with uBlock Origin, Privacy Badger & other must-have tools.
intro: Browser extensions can either protect or compromise your privacy. This comprehensive checklist helps you audit existing extensions, configure essential privacy tools like uBlock Origin, and build a secure extension stack that blocks trackers without sacrificing functionality.

items.why: Many extensions request excessive permissions that allow them to read all website data, access browsing history, or modify web pages unnecessarily.
items.howTo: Go to chrome://extensions or about:addons, click each extension, and review permissions. Remove extensions requesting 'Read and change all your data on websites' unless absolutely necessary.

items.task: Verify extensions are from official stores only
items.why: Sideloaded extensions bypass security reviews and may contain malware or privacy-violating code that steals personal data.
items.howTo: Check extension sources in browser settings. Remove any extensions installed from.crx files or third-party sites. Only use Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons, or Edge Add-ons.

items.task: Uninstall extensions you haven't used in 30+ days
items.why: Unused extensions create unnecessary attack surface and may run background processes that consume resources or collect data silently.
items.howTo: List all extensions with last-used dates. Remove any unused for over a month. Consider bookmarking useful but rarely-used extensions instead of keeping them installed.

items.task: Verify remaining extensions have 4+ star ratings and recent updates
items.why: Low-rated or abandoned extensions often have security vulnerabilities, compatibility issues, or poor privacy practices that developers won't fix.
items.howTo: Check each extension's store page for ratings, review count, and last update date. Replace extensions with <4 stars or no updates in 6+ months.

items.task: Research extension developers and their privacy policies
items.why: Unknown developers or extensions without privacy policies may collect and sell your browsing data to third parties without disclosure.
items.howTo: Click developer links, check their other extensions, and read privacy policies. Prefer extensions from known privacy-focused developers or open-source projects.

items.task: Install and configure uBlock Origin with optimal filter lists
items.why: uBlock Origin blocks ads, trackers, and malware more effectively than other blockers while using less memory and maintaining better performance.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin from official store. Enable EasyList, EasyPrivacy, uBlock filters, and regional lists for your location. Enable 'Prevent WebRTC from leaking local IP address'.

items.task: Install Privacy Badger for intelligent tracker blocking
items.why: Privacy Badger learns which domains track you across sites and automatically blocks them, complementing static filter lists with dynamic protection.
items.howTo: Install Privacy Badger from EFF. Enable 'Send Do Not Track header' and 'Prevent WebRTC from leaking local IP address'. Let it learn for a few days before adjusting settings.

items.task: Install Decentraleyes to block CDN tracking
items.why: Major CDNs like Google Fonts and jQuery can track you across websites. Decentraleyes serves local copies to prevent this tracking.
items.howTo: Install Decentraleyes and enable it. No configuration needed - it works automatically. Complements uBlock Origin by handling CDN resources it doesn't block.

items.task: Install ClearURLs to remove tracking parameters
items.why: URLs often contain tracking parameters that follow you across sites. ClearURLs automatically removes these while preserving functionality.
items.howTo: Install ClearURLs extension. Enable all default rules and check 'Allow domain blocking' for enhanced protection. Works silently in background.

items.task: Install Cookie AutoDelete for automatic cookie cleanup
items.why: Persistent cookies enable long-term tracking. Cookie AutoDelete removes cookies when you close tabs while maintaining login sessions for whitelisted sites.
items.howTo: Install Cookie AutoDelete. Set cleanup delay to 15 seconds. Whitelist essential sites like email, banking. Enable 'Clean cookies from Open Tabs on Startup'.

items.task: Enable HTTPS-only mode or install HTTPS Everywhere
items.why: Unencrypted HTTP connections expose your browsing data to network eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.
items.howTo: For Firefox/Chrome: Enable built-in HTTPS-only mode in Privacy settings. For older browsers: Install HTTPS Everywhere extension and enable 'Encrypt All Sites Eligible'.

items.task: Restrict extension permissions using site access controls
items.why: Even trusted extensions don't need access to every website. Limiting access reduces privacy risks if extensions are compromised.
items.howTo: In extension settings, change from 'On all sites' to 'On click' or 'On specific sites'. Configure per-site permissions for extensions that need specific site access.

items.task: Configure Firefox container tabs or Chrome profiles
items.why: Containers isolate browsing contexts, preventing cross-site tracking and separating work, personal, and social browsing activities.
items.howTo: Firefox: Install Multi-Account Containers. Create containers for shopping, social media, work. Chrome: Use separate browser profiles with different extension sets.

items.task: Install DuckDuckGo Privacy Essentials or similar
items.why: Search engines track queries and clicks. Privacy-focused search extensions provide protection while improving search privacy grades.
items.howTo: Install DuckDuckGo Privacy Essentials or Startpage extension. Set as default search in browser. Enable tracker blocking and privacy grade features.

items.task: Configure password manager extension with secure settings
items.why: Built-in browser password managers lack advanced security features. Dedicated extensions provide better encryption and security auditing.
items.howTo: Install Bitwarden or 1Password extension. Enable two-factor authentication, auto-lock after 15 minutes, and secure password generation with 16+ characters.

items.task: Test for extension conflicts and compatibility issues
items.why: Multiple privacy extensions can conflict, causing websites to break or reducing overall protection effectiveness.
items.howTo: Disable extensions one by one if sites break. Check uBlock Origin logger for blocked resources. Adjust filter lists or whitelist specific elements rather than disabling extensions.

items.task: Export and backup all extension configurations
items.why: Losing extension settings means reconfiguring everything from scratch and potentially weaker privacy protection during setup.
items.howTo: Export uBlock Origin settings, Privacy Badger data, and other extension configs. Save to encrypted cloud storage or local backup. Document custom filter rules.

pro_tips: Use a privacy-focused browser as your default for maximum privacy - it includes many of these protections built-in without needing multiple extensions.
Enable extension sync only for trusted extensions - malicious extensions can use sync to spread across your devices.
Test websites in private/incognito mode first when troubleshooting - this helps identify if extensions are causing issues.
Keep extension count under 10 total - too many extensions slow down browsing and increase attack surface significantly.
Update extensions manually rather than auto-update - this lets you review changes and avoid potentially compromised updates.
